method: Two independent Minecraft protocol clients issued real server commands and container clicks without ProtocolLib. The probe compared every top slot by type or custom model, quantity, caption, and all lore lines against independently decoded native packets, with clean completion from both clients. Every retained input and runtime log was hashed after server exit.
coverage: Nine packed indicator roles on a mixed custom block and vehicle item, using the actual page output, with one-role information pages, no-role native output and zero/disabled/shadowed/manual/visual-only inputs.

Independent rewards, conditional block drops and crop stage drops, inline and aliased series seeds, ore, surface, cave floor and ceiling, combined trunk and leaf, creature drop, caught material, finite fuels and returned container; real labels and lore checked.

Twenty-three independently numbered block sources were read to the final detail page. The source page controls, normal recipe buttons, Back, independent viewers, protected input, passive shift/right clicks, protected inspections and pristine player inventory were checked.

Live style override preserves a custom icon model and canonical original item; invalid selector/absent custom icon retain the preceding published definition and view. Generation and world switches are independently reloaded, then one reward is moved between subjects and the original config restored.

Colored plain and series seed names and the accepted custom fuel name are displayed alongside stable IDs. One fuel caption has 147 code points, including a supplementary character at a wrapping boundary. The complete caption was recovered from live native lore and no damaged surrogate/replacement appeared.
limits: Native inventory contents, tooltips and interactions were verified without a graphical client. These fixtures checked the accuracy of the configured source descriptions and did not measure drop frequencies or generate world terrain.
optional_protocol_scope: The nine-build player matrix ran without ProtocolLib. Spigot 1.21.11 and Paper 26.3 repeated the same player scenario with the official ProtocolLib binary loaded.
public_example_scope: Each build loaded the starter, pottery, showroom, published river example and a private creature fixture. At the normal plugin entry points, checks identified the river item sources and crafted output, then observed the exact direct and rule-based items and quantities on a real creature death event. A separate core process on each build ran the historical 49-assertion suite with its original 12 starting items.

offline_reward_checks.scope: Static reward projection of actual loaded BlocksAdder definitions used by catalog pages, including unique short reference resolution
coverage: General reward tables: broken vanilla material, caught-item vanilla material, native entity enum vs namespaced persistent tag, unrestricted source and invalid literal targets, zero chance suppressed, actor/permission/exact worlds and replacement details, duplicate independent same-table rolls retained.

Conditional block rewards: canonical selected block vs vanilla material, declaring-namespace output, BREAK age zero only, zero maximum amount, earlier fallible entry retained, guaranteed positive vanilla drop blocks a later custom drop, independent percent/Fortune/filters.

Crop: actual crop-series normalization, hidden alias suppressed, actual seed identity for conditionals, inline mature harvest/break and harvest-only with configured loots, seed refund/stage graphics absent; active/disabled flags, empty/missing output edges, first-positive order, reachable ages and prior rule decrease, actorless environmental tool and Fortune restrictions.

Creature: direct configured custom drop multiplicity and amount, replacement policy, generic matching separate, vanilla outputs do not produce a badge. Optional permission/default killer in general death rule. world.enabled false retains reward hints.

Registry: global unique short key, two- and three-namespace ambiguity, exact lookup precedes any fallback with stable object identity, unknown exact/short and null. Strict world-drop string amount/arity.
limits: In-process JVM per actual endpoint SDK. Fixture-local Material enum supplies traits normally fetched from the running Bukkit registry. Real Creature EntityType, Bukkit MemoryConfiguration, CropSchemas, ContentRegistry, both loot parsers, normalized source projection and immutable catalog output come from endpoint SDK or frozen plugin JAR. No network client, live server, NBT provider, material registry, item or loot evaluation was executed.

Events, generated worlds, saved placements, external entity persistent IDs and other plugins may alter drops at runtime. Filter descriptions express the configured conditions, not the probability that an arbitrary action actually awards an item. Earlier conditional world/NBT filter correlations are not inferred. Public NBT lore reports condition count only.

offline_generation_and_fuel_checks.entry: Production RecipeSources.load -> normal reward, generation and vehicle providers -> private index builder/wrap/pagination -> RecipeSources.forItem. Real production classes and collector from exact JAR; test class in same package; no server or client.
offline_generation_and_fuel_checks.fixture_scope: Bukkit MemoryConfiguration sections and published ContentRegistry built directly in memory; custom materials used for the offline fixture. No world placement or vehicle refueling event was executed.

diagnostic.reason: The initial combined fixture added four item definitions to the historical 12-item setup. Its example assertions passed, but the core startup count correctly failed. The retained final runs use separate processes for the example and the original core suite.

final_caption_checks.entry: Real packaged RecipeSources.load/forItem, crop+fuel providers and Text.plain. Direct edge cases invoked that JAR's private wrap by reflection. Only fixtures were in-memory Bukkit MemoryConfiguration and item/vehicle definitions. No mocked plugin classes, generated ItemStacks, server or client.
checks: Actual custom seed/fuel show canonical source ID plus English prefix/stripped caption, preserving wide letters, accents, emoji, literal unrecognized ampersand text and spaces. Standard, alternate and extended hex color sequences are stripped. Color-only source label has no caption.

Reconstructed both MiB-sized unbroken UTF-8 values from all real badge pages, with exact UTF-16 equality and no split surrogate. All wrapped lines measured up to 68 Unicode code points including indent, real pages held 16 lines except the last, and rebuilding yielded identical content.

Normal and two-space-indented wrapping at one before, on and after the line-width boundary tested NBSP, narrow NBSP, thin/zero-width/ideographic spaces, tab, combining mark and emoji ZWJ. All non-ASCII space sequences reconstructed verbatim. Interior ASCII runs are preserved; ASCII glue at a soft wrap can become the line transition. CR/LF boundaries produce separate lines. Units are Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters or pixels.

Both runtimes independently disassembled the packaged RecipeSourceRow.display: writes badge stacks with Inventory.setItem, without CatalogView.put/action registration; two distinct source-detail controls are earlier/later. Native clicks and rendered appearance are outside the offline fixture.

static_research.scope: Read-only inspection of the original recipe result selection, source and fuel information, and configurable styles. The recipe skin and resource pack delivery studies are follow-up research.
